Title: App For Participating at the Vienna Night Run

If you want to participate at the Vienna Night Run, you need to select a starting block first.
After that, you run for 5km and measure the time.
If you can do it in less than 25 minutes, you are good.
If not, you need to train and check until you have achieved this goal.
After that, you can get your starting number.
Depending on when your work day ends, you have to find out whether you can go there from home, or need to leave directly from work.
If more than one hour is left between your starting time and the end of your workday, you can go there from home.
Else, you need to leave directly from work.
While running at the Night Run, you run and drink at the same time.
In the end, you receive your final running time.

Some of the above information you have to enter into the app, some of the information is collected by fitness gadgets.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

result.rule: When the description states a specific activity, decision, or outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN element with wording that preserves the described action and its object or result; do not substitute a related but different action or outcome.

When the description states a specific business trigger or process outcome for a start or end event: Label the corresponding BPMN event with a concise phrase that preserves that stated trigger or outcome, rather than using a generic label such as “start” or “end”.

When the description names an activity or outcome with multiple stated actions, alternatives, or a distinguishing object or participant.: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or event so its described scope remains identifiable. Preserve materially stated actions, alternatives, and objects or participants; do not substitute a broader or different action or add unsupported details.

When the description states a core activity and separately describes a condition or later outcome that marks its completion: Label the BPMN activity with its core action and object; do not add the separately stated completion condition or later outcome to the activity label.
